claim: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected simple graph with \(d=|V|\ge3\), make every vertex a boundary vertex, replace every edge by an interval of common length \(\ell>0\), and let \(\Lambda_G(\lambda)\) be the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for \(-u''=\lambda u\). For an odd integer \(n\ge1\), put \(\lambda_0=(n\pi/\ell)^2\) and define the sharp local pole coefficient \[C_*(G)=\lim_{\lambda\to\lambda_0,\ \lambda\ne\lambda_0}|\lambda-\lambda_0|\,\sigma_{\min}(\Lambda_G(\lambda)).\]If \(Q(G)=D(G)+A(G)\) is the signless Laplacian and \(q_{\min}(G)\) its least eigenvalue, then \[C_*(G)=\frac{2\lambda_0}{\ell}\,q_{\min}(G).\]Hence \(C_*(G)>0\) exactly when \(G\) is non-bipartite. Among all simple \(d\)-vertex all-boundary equilateral decorations, the complete graph \(K_d\) uniquely maximizes the pole coefficient, with \[C_*(K_d)=\frac{2\lambda_0}{\ell}(d-2).\]At an even Dirichlet resonance the corresponding coefficient is \(0\). For the four-boundary triangle-with-one-pendant-edge resonator used as the degree-four example by Do--Kuchment--Ong, \(q_{\min}=(5-\sqrt{17})/2\), so \(K_4\) improves the sharp pole coefficient by the exact factor \((5+\sqrt{17})/2\).

correctness.rationale: The exact edge solution yields \(\Lambda_G(k^2)=k[\sin(k\ell)]^{-1}(A-\cos(k\ell)D)\). At odd \(k_0\ell=n\pi\), the finite matrix tends to \(Q=D+A\) and the scalar factor satisfies \(|k^2-k_0^2||k/\sin(k\ell)|\to2k_0^2/\ell\). The complement identity and a missing-edge Rayleigh vector prove the unique \(K_d\) optimizer. A standalone checker confirms finite cases and resonance limits.

originality.rationale: The claim is limited to the sharp local pole coefficient and its fixed-\(d\) optimization in the all-boundary equilateral simple-graph class. The general gap mechanism and odd-cycle sufficient construction are prior work.
residual_risks: An equivalent residue identity may occur in literature using M-function or boundary-triple language rather than Dirichlet-to-Neumann terminology.
The source paper's full design problem allows more general decorations, so the present theorem closes only the all-boundary equilateral simple-graph subclass.
The sharp local pole coefficient is not by itself an exact host-independent spectral-gap width.
